question: After the credentialed lifecycle proof passes, should Crabbox ship this direct provider with persistent GitHub Codespaces scope, operator billing exposure, and claim-authorized remote deletion?
rationale: Source and tests can establish the intended ownership mechanics, but only maintainers can accept the permanent credential, cost, and destructive-resource boundary for a first-party provider.

options.title: Accept after live proof
options.body: Merge after exact-head delete and dirty-retain lifecycle evidence demonstrates the documented zero-residue and preservation guarantees.

options.title: Make deletion opt-in
options.body: Change the default to stop and retain, requiring trusted configuration for destructive release cleanup before shipping.

options.title: Pause the provider
options.body: Leave the linked issue and PR open until a maintainer can own Codespaces credentials, quota, recurring validation, and incident recovery.

recommendation.title: Accept after live proof
recommendation.body: Merge after exact-head delete and dirty-retain lifecycle evidence demonstrates the documented zero-residue and preservation guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current ownership hardening and have repeatedly framed the remaining live-proof and destructive-cleanup gates.
